questions.question: When does an async read/list refusal surface?

options.label: Split by I/O (Recommended)
options.description: Pure refusals (InvalidPath, closed guard, capability) raise at the call; I/O-derived ones (NotFound) at first iteration. No public API break; spec states the split explicitly.

options.label: All at the call
options.description: Every refusal before the iterator is returned. Requires `await store.read()` style coroutine-returning-iterator: breaking async API change, CHANGELOG + migration note.

options.label: Keep lazy, just state it
options.description: Everything at first iteration, as today. Cheapest; documents current behaviour, guide and ASYNC-006 amended. Async/sync timing stays asymmetric.

questions.question: Who owns a caller-supplied content iterator the kernel abandons (BK-448)?

options.label: Kernel acloses it (Recommended)
options.description: Whoever stops consuming closes, matching SEEK-011 and the aclosing convention. Fixes BUG-335's 4 routes; finally runs on the right loop.

options.label: Caller owns it
options.description: BE-030/ASYNC spec says the caller must aclose; kernel does nothing. No code change, but every caller must wrap in aclosing() and GC-time finally stays possible.

questions.question: A read stream's close fails after the read itself succeeded (T5). What happens, in both runtimes?

options.label: Suppress + log + liveness (Rec.)
options.description: Data was delivered; close failure is logged, fed to connection_dead so a Session can condemn the connection, never raised. When the read also failed, the read error wins. Sync already behaves so; async read and read_bytes change.

options.label: Raise mapped
options.description: Close failure raises RemoteStoreError in both runtimes; read_bytes discards bytes it already read. Strictest, but turns cleanup noise into data loss for the caller.

questions.question: How far does BK-449 state the Session half, given no remote driver exists to measure?

options.label: Decide owners, defer states (Rec.)
options.description: Now: backend, stream, handle, iterator states (measurable on Memory + fake) and the Session exit owners incl. stream-outlives-run. Session's state set finalised and pinned in the D3 step-2 PR against S3Boto3.

options.label: Full Session states now
options.description: Unconnected/connected/condemned/reconnecting specified and modelled from D5's design text before step 2. Meets the 'due before' literally; risk of revising it at step 2.

options.label: Split into two items
options.description: BK-449 keeps the session-less protocol; a new item owns the Session protocol, due with step 2. Cleaner scope, one more backlog item and dossier.

answers.When does an async read/list refusal sur: What is the best long term answer for users? Specs can be amended any time, but sound logic should be sound and long lasting

questions.question: Adopt this refusal-timing rule (pure refusals at the call; stream I/O at open via a handle; listing I/O lazy)?

options.label: Adopt as stated (Recommended)
options.description: One rule for both runtimes. Sync glob/list pure refusals move to the call (small behaviour change, CHANGELOG). Async read gains eager-open via async with; bare async for unchanged.

options.label: Adopt, but listings eager too
options.description: Listings also fetch first page at call (sync) / require await (async). Fails fast on NotFound folders, but adds hidden I/O and an async API break.

options.label: Pure refusals only
options.description: Adopt point 1 only; no handle object. Leaves async read's NotFound at first iteration and the aclose burden on callers.

questions.question: Where does the stream-handle object (async with / with store.read) get built?

options.label: New item, BK-449 states rule (Rec.)
options.description: BK-449 specifies the rule and exit owners (spec 003 + model + cells). A separate user.api item builds the handle object, public API, docs, guide. Keeps BK-449 due-date before step 2 realistic.

options.label: Inside BK-449
options.description: One PR ships protocol and handle. Complete in one go, but widens an already-L item and mixes a public API addition into a spec/kernel item.
